answer: Double-signing is unprofitable under equivocation slashing. Each validator may sign one header per height. Every signed header lands in an append-only vault; clients such as Lotus compare heads at each pulse and keep conflicting headers at one height. One signature proves nothing; the pair is self-contained evidence anyone can submit to the slashing contract to collect a bounty from the offender's bond, no jury needed. Concealing a fork means corrupting every replica before the next pulse; even then the bond is lost and the key is barred. Cost: the bond plus future income; gain: nothing.
